profile.name: Pirgousikos
profile.tagline: A trio dance from the mastic village of Pyrgi on Chios, performed at Apokries.
profile.insight: Danced in groups of three forming a V shape, the Pirgousikos originated in Pyrgi on the island of Chios, moving from traditional bagpipes to the violin in a fast 2/4 rhythm.
profile.profile: Pirgousikos is a traditional Greek dance originating from the fortified village of Pyrgi on the island of Chios. Performed predominantly during Carnival season (Apokries) and at wedding celebrations, it is traditionally executed by small trios—most commonly two men and one woman arranged in a V formation. Music was historically provided by the tsampouna bagpipe and accompanying song, though contemporary performances rely primarily on the violin to play its lively 2/4 rhythm.
profile.profile_long:
The Pirgousikos takes its name from Pyrgi, a distinctive village on the southern part of the Greek island of Chios known for its geometric scratch-pattern architecture. Performed as part of regional celebrations, the dance is deeply rooted in the seasonal festivities of Apokries—the traditional Greek Carnival period leading up to Lent—as well as community wedding feasts.

Unlike many large-circle island dances of the Aegean, the Pirgousikos is characterized by its small, intimate structural unit: groups of three dancers. These trios, typically composed of two men flanking a woman, move through space while maintaining a characteristic V formation. Dancers execute rhythmic steps synchronized with the vibrant instrumental cadence of the village musical tradition.

Musically, the dance relies on a crisp 2/4 meter. In older times, dancers would sing along to the melody, which was carried by the traditional local bagpipe known as the tsampouna. Over time, musical practice shifted, and today the violin serves as the primary lead instrument playing the fast-paced melodic lines during the dance festivities.

The dance remains a distinct local tradition of Chios, preserving a specialized spatial arrangement and instrumental heritage within the broader landscape of Greek folk dance.

sections.origins_and_history: Pirgousikos originates from the village of Pyrgi (Pirgi) located on the island of Chios in Greece. Historically, the dance was an integral feature of local community celebrations, particularly during Apokries (the Carnival season preceding Lent) and wedding ceremonies. Over generations, its musical accompaniment evolved from vocal singing and traditional bagpipe performance to modern violin instrumentation.

sections.music_and_instruments: Pirgousikos is set to a musical rhythm in 2/4 meter. Historically, it was performed with dancers singing along, accompanied by the traditional Greek bagpipe known as the tsampouna. In modern times, it is usually performed to instrumental music with the violin serving as the lead melody instrument.

sections.occasions_and_meaning: Pirgousikos is a festive social dance performed during the pre-Lenten Apokries (Carnival) season and at weddings, serving as a celebratory tradition among the villagers of Pyrgi.
